'''Brian Keith Tanner'''  [[Chartered Physicist|CPhys]], [[Royal Society of Arts|FRSA]], [[Institute of Physics|FInstP]], [[Higher Education Academy|FHEA]] is a British physicist, currently Emeritus Professor of Physics and former Dean of Knowledge Transfer at [[Durham University]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dur.ac.uk/physics/staff/profiles/?id=556|title=Prof BK Tanner - Durham University|work=dur.ac.uk}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Brian Tanner grew up in Northamptonshire, attending [[Wellingborough School|Wellingborough Grammar School]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.grahamtall.co.uk/wgs1955/1958%20reunion/1958_reunion_photograph.htm|title=1958 Reunion Photographs OGs at Wellingborough Grammar School|work=grahamtall.co.uk}}</ref> He studied undergraduate physics at [[University of Oxford|Balliol College, University of Oxford]], where he went on to graduate with a [[DPhil]] in 1971 on 'X-ray diffraction topography; methods and applications'.<ref>{{cite thesis|url=http://ethos.bl.uk/OrderDetails.do?uin=uk.bl.ethos.474552|title=British Library EThOS : Thesis Details - X-Ray Diffraction Topography: Methods and Applications.|author=Tanner, B. K.|work=bl.uk|year=1971|type=Ph.D}}</ref>

== Career ==
Tanner is best known for research and business applications of X-ray [[diffraction topography]].<ref name="vitae.ac.uk"/>
Tanner has worked at the Department of Physics at [[Durham University]] since 1973, where he was made Professor of Physics in 1996 and was the University Dean of Knowledge Transfer from 2008 to 2016 until his retirement.<ref name="dur.ac.uk"/> He has published over 375 papers in international peer-reviewed journals and 4 books.<ref name="kromek.com">{{cite web|url=http://www.kromek.com/aboutus_theboard.asp|title=Kromek - About us - The Board|work=kromek.com|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150307125211/http://www.kromek.com/aboutus_theboard.asp|archivedate=7 March 2015}}</ref>
In 1978 he co-founded Bede Scientific Instruments Ltd, since 2008 owned by Jordan Valley Semiconductors.<ref name="dur.ac.uk"/> From 2003 to 2015 he was a non-executive director of radiation detection solutions company Kromek, supplying medical imaging, civil nuclear, security screening and homeland security markets.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Home |url=https://www.kromek.com/ |access-date=2025-11-25 |website=Kromek |language=en}}</ref>

Professor Tanner was the first Director of the North East Centre for Science Enterprise, and served as chief scientific advisor of the North East Technology Park ([[NETPark]]) and chaired the County Durham Economic Partnership.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.northeasttechnologypark.com/innovation-community/chief-scientific-advisor|title=Chief Scientific Advisor|author=Andrea Stephenson|work=northeasttechnologypark.com|access-date=28 January 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150101121019/http://www.northeasttechnologypark.com/innovation-community/chief-scientific-advisor|archive-date=1 January 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.countydurhampartnership.co.uk/Pages/EcP-Home.aspx |title=Economic Partnership |access-date=28 January 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151201044843/http://www.countydurhampartnership.co.uk/Pages/EcP-Home.aspx |archive-date=1 December 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Awards and honours ==
Tanner is a [[Chartered Physicist]], a [[Fellow of the Institute of Physics]], [[Fellow of the Higher Education Academy]], and [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Arts]]
Jointly awarded the 2005 Barrett Award of the [[International Center for Diffraction Data]]. Awarded the [[Queen's Award for Enterprise Promotion]] in 2012 for his work in promoting enterprise and business in the North East.<ref name="dur.ac.uk"/> In 2014, the [[Institute of Physics]] awarded Tanner the [[Gabor Medal]] for distinguished work in the application of physics in an industrial, commercial or business context.<ref name="instituteofphysics"/>

== Personal life ==
Married to Ruth Tanner, formerly a Trustee and Deputy President of the [[Workers' Educational Association]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wea.org.uk/governance/|title=Workers' Educational Association (WEA) - Adult Learning Course Provider UK|work=wea.org.uk}}</ref> and currently secretary of the Cobweb Orchestra, about which she published a history in 2013.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cobweborchestra.org.uk/about/|title=About – The Cobweb Orchestra|website=cobweborchestra.org.uk|language=en-GB|access-date=2018-07-03}}</ref> He has two sons: Rob is a teacher and Director of Cross-Curricular Learning at St Albans School <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.st-albans.herts.sch.uk/press-release/st-albans-school-sixth-form-physicists-scoop-top-prizes-npl-school-science-film-challenge/|access-date=2021-06-08|website=www.st-albans.herts.sch.uk |title=St Albans School }}</ref> and Tom is a climate change academic at SOAS University of London.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Thomas Tanner {{!}} SOAS University of London |url=https://www.soas.ac.uk/about/thomas-tanner |url-status=live |access-date=2025-11-25 |website=www.soas.ac.uk |language=en}}</ref>
